matched_finding.description: In Table 2, the omnibus test for sadness shows p=.033, but in the text it is reported as p=.003. This is a discrepancy that needs clarification. If the correct p-value is .033, this is closer to the significance threshold and more concerning given the lack of multiple comparison correction. If .003 is correct, the table has an error.

matched_finding.description: The authors report that 'desire to die from pre to post significantly decreased slightly, t(32)=2.23, p=.033,' but Table 1 shows the change as +0.20 (from 0.82 to 1.03), which would indicate an increase, not a decrease. This is contradictory and raises concerns about the accuracy of the reported statistics.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Creates internal contradiction detectable within the paper

ground_truth.description: Changed 'two-week' to 'one-week' in episode definition but all other references say 'two weeks' / '14 days' — cross-section inconsistency

matched_finding.description: Suicide attempt episodes used a one-week period prior to the attempt, while ideation, depressed mood, and positive mood episodes used two-week periods. Later in the methods, the authors describe using 14 days (two weeks) for all episode types in the primary analyses. This inconsistency in the description is confusing and raises questions about whether the episode windows were truly comparable across conditions.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: No random slopes with marginal p-values — must know Barr et al recommendations
ground_truth.original_snippet: Models with the full set of random slopes did not converge; therefore, only a by-participant slope of episode type was included in the final model.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: Models with the full set of random slopes did not converge; therefore, no random slopes were included in the final model.
ground_truth.description: Removed all random slopes (kept only intercepts) — fails to account for participant variability in episode effects; inflates Type I error per Barr et al (2013); key p-values near .05 may become false positives

matched_finding.subcategory: Random effects structure not maximal as planned
matched_finding.description: The authors stated they would follow Barr et al. (2013) recommendations for maximal random effects structures, but for Analysis 2, the models with random slopes did not converge, so all random slopes were dropped. This is a substantial deviation from the planned analysis that could affect both Type I error rates and the validity of the results. Dropping all random slopes (rather than systematically simplifying) may lead to anti-conservative estimates for the interaction effects, which are the primary results of Analysis 2.
matched_finding.quote: Models with the full set of random slopes did not converge; therefore, no random slopes were included in the final model.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Claims all 27 had attempt data but only 15 did — must check if 27=27 makes sense given design
ground_truth.original_snippet: Among these 27 participants, 15 had data from at least one reported suicide attempt; the other 12 participants contributed data from non-suicide attempt episodes and were still included in the analyses.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: Among these 27 participants, all had data from at least one reported suicide attempt.
ground_truth.description: Concealed that only 15/27 (56%) had attempt SMS data — hides selection bias in who contributes to the critical attempt vs non-attempt comparisons

matched_finding.description: Only 46% of reported episodes had corresponding SMS data, and data availability depended on technical factors (phone type, encryption settings, cloud backups, device age). This creates a non-random pattern of missing data that could systematically bias results. For example, more recent episodes may be more likely to have SMS data, and recency could be confounded with other factors (e.g., current mental health status, maturity, treatment history).
matched_finding.quote: a number of iPhone users had encryption settings on their phones that prevented third-party iPhone software from accessing text data
